title: What Happens When a Magnet Falls Through a Copper Pipe?
description:
It falls in slow motion—even though copper is not a permanent magnet.

The magnet falls slowly because its changing magnetic field induces eddy currents in the copper, whose magnetic effect opposes the change.

This is Lenz’s law. Energy is converted into a small amount of heat in the pipe.

Cutting a slot along the pipe weakens the circulating currents and lets the magnet fall faster.
